_numbering_note: catalog_number pending the base/hybrid renumbering (see gdd-culture-emergence-and-territory.md); csv_id is the authoritative key for now.
sub_palette: germanic (norse) backbone + classical (hellenic) overlay (cross-family blend, Germanic-leaning)

blend.backbone: germanic (norse register: konungr/jarl, dithematic -r/-son names, ai>ei and i/u-umlaut, w- lost before round vowels, the axe-bearing hird and the sea-keel)
blend.overlay: classical (hellenic: the polis and the agora, the archon/basileus civic register, pitch-accent learning, -os/-on/-polis toponyms, the philosophers and the fleets)
blend.lean: Germanic-heavy - a Norse warrior-elite (the axe-bearers of Miklagardr, the Varangian Guard enthroned) ruling over the Hellenic city-civilization: the sea-raiding hird holds the crown and the guard, the learned poleis and their fleets endure and serve beneath.

_note: NEW cross-family hybrid under the base/hybrid model. BASE_01 Thiodmark (Germanic) x BASE_07 (Hellenic/Classical). CIV/CLAN DECIDED by inheritance: Germanic base = Clanhold, Greek/Classical base = Civilized, and any Civ parent -> Civ, so Hellmark is Civilized (feudal). Concept: a Norse warrior-elite - the axe-bearers of Miklagardr, the Varangian Guard enthroned - that came as sea-raiders and mercenary guard to the Hellenic poleis and made themselves kings over the city-civilization (a Norse-Byzantine fusion: northern jarls over the philosophers' city-states and their fleets). Backbone = Germanic (NORSE: the ruling war-elite and the hird, the konungr/jarl register, dithematic -r/-son names); overlay/substrate = Classical (HELLENIC: the polis and the agora, the archon/basileus civic register, the learned populace, the fleets, -os/-on/-polis toponyms). Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Old Norse and Greek registers (allowed, catalog 5.3); DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon from both parents (NORSE reflexes primary, Hellenic variants secondary), never real Norse/Greek gods. The Norse reflexes come from family_germanic theonym_ancestors (the norse column); the Hellenic morphs follow achillean's deity-morph register. PROVISIONAL: alignment (Neutral/Lawful) is a per-hybrid design choice pending the alignment pass - the Norse war-oath and hird-loyalty meet the Hellenic civic law and the basileus' settled order; the older raider layer reads Neutral, the enthroned guard-and-polis order reads Lawful. Register choice: this Germanic-base hybrid uses the NORSE reflexes (Miklagardr = the Great City), per the Varangian-Guard rationale - flag for Jedidiah if a uniform Germanic register is wanted instead. [UPDATE 2026-06-27: all human cultures allow Lawful/Neutral/Chaotic (per-hybrid alignment restriction removed). Ruler/domain DISPLAY titles are now English (or an approved foreign term); conlang titles moved to ruler_native/domain_native for NPC dialogue. Deities unchanged: canonical Agrippan pantheon via the per-family morph method.]

phonology.palette: Germanic (Norse) backbone - heavy root-initial stress, sharp stops p/t/k b/d/g, retained th/dh, the nominative -r, ai>ei and au>ey, i- and u-umlaut, w- lost before round vowels (Wod- > Od-), dithematic compounding and -son/-dottir - meeting a Hellenic overlay: vowel-rich a e i o u with long e/o, aspirates th/ph/kh, sibilant s, the civic -os/-on/-eus/-e endings and -polis. Per the CSV: a pitch accent merged with stress accent (the Hellenic pitch settling under the heavy Norse root-stress); grammar is SVO with strong/weak verbs carrying complex aspects (the Germanic verb-system over the Greek aspectual frame). Theophoric on the Norse reflexes (Thulr-, Orlund-) with Hellenic variants (Tulrio-, Orlandro-).
phonology.phonotactics: CVC; Norse clusters (st, sk, sp, br, kn, hl, hr) and the nominative -r meeting Hellenic onset-clusters (kt, pt, ps, th, ph, kh) and the open vowel-final -os/-on; heavy initial stress with a Hellenic penultimate pull; dithematic Norse names over -polis / -os / -eia civic toponyms.

sound_changes: Hellenic civic endings drop into the Norse nominative: final -os/-on/-e/-a>0, the root takes the Norse -r (potamos>potamr, oros>orr, asty>astr); very short roots also take -r
Hellenic aspirates and exotic onsets collapse into the Norse inventory: ph>f (lophos>lofr), kh>k (chrysos>krysr, rhachis>rakr), rh>r (rhoos>royr); th retained (shared by both)
Norse root-initial stress on all words; the Hellenic pitch-accent settles under the heavy Norse stress (pitch>stress); Norse clusters (st, sk, sp, br, kn, hl, hr) permitted
Norse-sourced roots keep their native shape: the -r nominative, i- and u-umlaut, ai>ei and au>ey, w- lost before round vowels; retain Norse dh and the Hellenic s
Hellenic ou/oi diphthongs reshape to Norse ey/oy (kleisoura>kleysr, huios>hui-); -ion endings>-inn (pedion>pedinn, elaion>elainn)
fusion_rules.source_tilt: sea/land/civic/material/staple words from Hellenic roots (the substrate poleis hold the coast, the polis, the marble and the vine: potamos>potamr, thalassa>thalassr, polis>pol, marmaros>marmr, sitos>sitr); kin-line/quality/abstract/rule/war words from Norse roots (the ruling hird: mikill, svartr, jarn, hross, forfadr); every chosen root then run through the one Norse-shaped sound-law so the split is inaudible at the surface

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Hellenic sea/land/civic/material roots + Norse kin/quality/rule/war roots, all run through one Norse-shaped sound-law (the -r nominative, dropped -os/-on, pitch>stress); portmanteaus mark the blended institutions and bloodline of the Varangian poleis.

morphology.patronymic_form: the Norse ruling stock carry the -son / -dottir patronymic and a dithematic lineage-name (the -ungr / -ingar line of the jarl-house); the Hellenic populace keep the -ides / -ades patronymic and the polis/deme demonym of origin; the throne fuses both - a konungr who also bears a basileus-title and a polis-seat.
morphology.compounding_rule: Norse dithematic ([quality|animal|resource](stem) + element: Jarn-borg, iron-fort; Svart-vidr, black-wood) layered over Hellenic civic compounds (feature/quality + -polis / linking -o-: Neapolis, Melanoros): the capital Miklagardr (the Great City), Jarnborg (the iron-fort), Thulrs-polis (Thulr's-city).

title_ladder.government: feudal (a Norse war-elite over the Hellenic poleis: the konungr-basileus and his jarl-kin at the crown, the hersar and eparchs over the city-provinces, the axe-bearing hird sworn to the throne; the archons and the strategoi of the fleets, the agora and the philosophers' schools serve beneath)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Norse ladder, ascending, with the Hellenic substrate co-titles beneath. Hersir (war-chief / sworn lord) barony over a Hersa-rad; Markgreifi (march-count) march over a Mork; Eparkr (Norse-borne form of the Greek eparch / provincial governor) county over an Eparkia; Hertogi (war-leader; *harja-tugon) duchy over a Hertogadaemi; Jarl (the great earl-prince) principality over a Jarlsriki; Konungr-Basileus (the king, fusing the Norse konungr and the Greek basileus) kingdom over a Konungsriki; Stori Basileus (the Great Basileus, king-of-kings; ON storr + Gk basileus) empire over the Megalriki (the 'great realm'). The conquered poleis keep their Hellenic archon (city-magistrate) and strategos (general / fleet-commander) beneath the Norse crown. The godi (priest) and the Hellenic hierophant stand outside the ladder. Rank titles fuse the real Old Norse and Greek registers (allowed).
title_ladder.heir: Konungs-barn (the king's child; the heir; the Hellenic Diadochos for the polis-line)
title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH (or an approved commonly-known foreign term where set in 'ruler'). The *_native conlang forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: the Norse ruling stock carry a dithematic name + -son / -dottir patronymic and a jarl-house lineage; the Hellenic populace carry a personal name + -ides patronymic + polis/deme demonym; order given-first.
people_name_convention.dual_register: the Norse war-elite keep Old Norse dithematic names (Thor-, Sig-, Har-, -steinn, -ulfr, -arr, with -son/-dottir); the Hellenic city-folk keep Greek names (the -on/-os/-eus stems with -ides patronymics and deme demonyms).
people_name_convention.theophoric: Norse devotional on the morphed god-reflexes (Thulrs-arr, Orlund-steinn); Hellenic devotional on the morphed stems (Tulrio-, Orlandro-, Numeno-): Tulriodoros (gift of Tulrios), Orlandrokles.

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - NORSE Germanic reflexes PRIMARY (family_germanic theonym_ancestors, the norse column), Hellenic variants SECONDARY (the Hellenic deity-morphs in achillean's register), never real Norse/Greek gods. Alignment PROVISIONAL (Neutral/Lawful): the Norse war-oath and hird-loyalty meet the Hellenic civic law and the basileus' settled order.
religion.the_one: Eitnir (Norse; Hellenic Aiternos) - the distant Ancient One, honored not petitioned

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers - Eitnir, Thulr the just, Orlund of the sworn war, Rjalta the merciful - and names the Chaotic powers fjandr (fiends) / daimones, warded and unworshipped; the hird-oath and the basileus' civic law bind alike, the enthroned guard and the ordered polis the social ideal
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: the ancestral war-dead (the disir and the deified jarls of the ruling house) and the city-heroes of the poleis (the heroon-dead); the great powers invoked at the hof-grove and the polis-temple situationally rather than worshipped wholesale
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon, and names the Lawful powers - and Eitnir - as the tyrant-gods to be defied.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers, warded as fjandr (Norse fiends) or -daimon (Hellenic demon), keep their morphs + an epithet: Maraxus -> Marhr the War-Brand (Hell. Maraxos the Tyrant-Flame); Vacidus -> Vakr the Unmaker (Hell. Vakidos-daimon); Lusanto -> Lusandr the Hoard-Worm (Hell. Lusandos the Drowner-of-Gold).
religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Hof (Norse grove-temple) or Hieron / Temenos (Hellenic sacred precinct) of [power]: 'the Hof of Thulr', 'the Temenos of Tulrios'.
religion.saints_pattern: the disir and the deified jarls (the war-dead of the ruling house, honored at the haugr / barrow) and the Hellenic heroes (Heros [name], venerated at a heroon / tomb-shrine in the poleis).

holy_symbol_motifs.Thulr: a sun-wheel over a crossed axe and scales
holy_symbol_motifs.Orlund: an iron axe crossed with an oath-ring
holy_symbol_motifs.Geyandr: the standing stones above the olive-terrace

banks_patterns.ships: the war-keel and the long-ship, named in Norse kennings and Hellenic virtue-names: 'the Wave-Stallion', 'Raven of Miklagardr', 'the Nike', 'Pride of the Thalassa'
banks_patterns.military_units: the Konungr's hird (the axe-bearing guard / Varangian-band) and the polis levies: 'the Hird of Miklagardr', 'the Axe-bearers', 'the Bronze Phalanx of the poleis'
banks_patterns.taverns: 'The [Adjective] [Noun]': 'The Amber Kylix', 'The Axe and Olive', 'The Golden Drekar'
banks_patterns.dungeons_ruins: sunken poleis and fallen Norse borgs: 'the Akropolis of [name]', 'the Sunken Hof', 'the Haugr of the Jarls', 'the broken Jarlsborg'

flagship_settlements: Miklagardr (the chief seat - the Great City)
Neapolis (the new polis of the substrate)
Akropolis-haugr (the citadel over the old barrow)
